scope: Desktop x86_64 memory feasibility measurement for segment-bounded Demucs separation. NOT a quality result and NOT an ARM measurement.
question: Rhythm Doctor must run standalone on the Norns. Demucs is the strongest licence-clean bass separator. Its widely quoted 3-7 GB requirement is for whole-track processing, and it processes in segments, so does peak memory scale with segment length rather than capture length?
verdict: NO. Segment length does not bound peak memory in the reference implementation. The hypothesis is refuted and Demucs is not viable on this device as-is.

method.input: v12-acquisition-120.wav, 45.0 s, the product's full capture bound

findings: Reducing the segment eightfold, from 7.8 s to 1 s, did not reduce peak RSS at all. Peak stayed within 1379-1490 MB and was HIGHEST at the smallest segment, while elapsed time rose more than fivefold.
The floor is already disqualifying: 483 MB to load the PyTorch runtime and the model, against roughly 470 MB available on the device with no swap, before any activation is allocated.
Peak is about three times the entire device budget.

Time was never the constraint. 27.1 s for a 45 s capture on a single desktop thread, and the product tolerates minutes for a stop-transport capture-and-paint workflow. Memory is the binding constraint.
qualifications: The 483 MB baseline includes the PyTorch runtime itself. A purpose-built ONNX implementation would not carry PyTorch, and the weights alone are 167.9 MB fp32 or about 84 MB fp16.

However, roughly 900 MB of activation memory did not respond to segment length, so the reference implementation does not stream. Making it fit would require a bespoke streaming ONNX implementation, which is substantial work with an uncertain outcome.
This is an x86_64 measurement. It establishes the algorithmic memory scale, not ARMv7 behaviour. PyTorch is in any case unavailable on armv7l, so the deployed path could never be this one.
No quality measurement was taken. This says nothing about whether Demucs would improve the BASS lane, only that it cannot run on the device in this form.
consequence: Separation-first is blocked on device footprint for the standalone requirement, not on quality or licence. The hypothesis that segment bounding would rescue it is refuted by measurement.
